# Lab 24.2: Partition & Cluster Recommendations

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a table that would benefit from partitioning, generate the query pattern the recommender looks for, then apply a recommendation and measure the bytes saved.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a large, unpartitioned table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS lab24 OPTIONS (location = 'US');

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab24.trips AS
SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE trip_start_timestamp &gt;= '2022-01-01';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Create a repeated filter pattern.** Run date-filtered queries every day for a few days (or schedule them):


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">for d in 2022-03-01 2022-06-01 2022-09-01 2023-01-01 2023-04-01; do
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --nouse_cache "SELECT company, SUM(fare) FROM lab24.trips WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '$d' GROUP BY company" &gt; /dev/null
done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Read the recommendation.** After the recommender runs (up to a day), open **Recommendations**. A **Partition** recommendation for `lab24.trips` suggests `DAY` partitioning on `trip_start_timestamp`, with estimated slot-hours saved.

4. **[SQL] Apply it by creating a new table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab24.trips_partitioned
PARTITION BY DATE(trip_start_timestamp)
CLUSTER BY company
AS SELECT * FROM lab24.trips;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[SQL] Measure the saving.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT company, SUM(fare) FROM lab24.trips WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-01-01' GROUP BY company;
SELECT company, SUM(fare) FROM lab24.trips_partitioned WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-01-01' GROUP BY company;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Compare bytes billed in **Job information**.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Repeated filters on one column |
| Recommendation | Partition and/or cluster column |
| Applying | New table with the suggested layout |
| Saving | Far fewer bytes per query |
